problem: Prior MARL work is mostly on grid-world or game environments with low-dimensional observations, while embodied navigation benchmarks are mostly single-agent. Existing communication-based MARL also discards all messages after each round, so agents lose information that may matter later and act short-sightedly.
motivation: Multi-agent systems matter for search-and-rescue, area coverage and similar tasks, but no visually rich, photo-realistic benchmark exists for studying collaboration. In partially observable navigation, past communication (e.g. an already-explored wrong room) is valuable for long-term planning, so agents should be able to store and recall it.
key_idea: Give each agent a private external memory of its past communication keys and values, and use it in a handshake (request/match/select/store) communication protocol trained with fully decentralized PPO, on a new multi-agent image-goal navigation dataset, CollaVN.
insight: Adding memory to communication gives clearly larger gains than communication alone. On CommonGoal N=2, overall SR is 17.69 (w/o com), 18.29 (w/o mem) and 21.52 (Ours), so communication without memory helps only marginally. Team-size gains are small (SR 21.52 to 23.10 from N=2 to 4), and SPL barely changes, which motivates the new SSR metric. The Ad-hoc results suggest fully decentralized learning with per-agent critics lets policies adapt to changed team sizes.
method: CollaVN dataset: built on iGibsonV1 with 572 buildings, Locobot agents, panoramic RGB, a 128x128 goal image and continuous velocity actions. Adds modules for safe multi-agent initialization, a panoramic camera and target-image generation. 1M/60K/120K train/val/test episodes, split by distance into easy/medium/hard.
Three task settings: CommonGoal (same goal image), SpecificGoal (different goal per agent), and Ad-hoCoop (team size changes between train and test, 2→3 or 3→2).

Map building module: each agent builds an egocentric map online from its observation and pose, with 256 visual-feature channels plus 4 channels (obstacle, explored area, trajectory, current location), following Active Neural SLAM.

Memory-augmented handshake communication: each agent creates query/key/value (256/256/2048-d MLPs) from its observation, its map and avg-pooled past values. It broadcasts only the query. Supporters match it against their current and all stored past keys, and scores and values are averaged over time.

Select and store: scores at or below the threshold η=1/N are zeroed, which decides who and when to communicate. The aggregated message ω goes to a GRU policy, and the agent then stores its own current key and value in its memory.
Fully decentralized PPO: each agent has its own actor and critic conditioned on its observation and received message. The reward is the geodesic distance reduction minus 0.05 per collision.
SSR metric: Success weighted by Step Ratio, T/min(T,T_kn), added alongside multi-agent SR, DTS and SPL because SPL is tiny and uninformative in this hard task.

setting.backbone: Pretrained ResNet18 observation encoder + map module + one-layer-MLP communication + GRU policy/value (trained with PPO)
setting.training_data: CollaVN train split: 125K episodes per subset (25 Gibson-tiny scenes, 5K episodes per scene), trained per team-size setting
setting.observation: egocentric panoramic RGB 3x512x128 + goal image RGB 3x128x128 + pose (for mapping)
setting.action_space: continuous 2-D normalized (translational, rotational) velocity in [-1,1]^2, max 70 cm/s and 180 deg/s, 1 s per step
setting.privileged: none (agents don't know each other's positions; pose estimates are used for mapping)

numbers.backbone: ResNet18 + map + memory-augmented comm + GRU, PPO
numbers.extra: team size N=2, T=80 steps, success radius 1 m

numbers_note: All results are on the paper's own CollaVN benchmark, which is not one of the canonical benchmarks. Per-difficulty (easy/medium/hard) numbers are also in the tables but omitted here. SR is in percent; SPL and SSR are printed as small decimals.
results: The memory-augmented communication model beats all baselines on every metric across all three MAVN settings. For CommonGoal N=2, overall SR is 21.52 vs 18.29 (MARL w/o mem), 17.69 (w/o com) and 16.37 (IL). Performance rises slightly with team size, and SpecificGoal is somewhat harder than CommonGoal. Absolute SR stays low (about 21-23%, only about 2-3% on hard episodes), so the task remains far from solved.
limitations: Absolute performance is low, especially on hard (5-10 m) episodes where SR is about 2-3%. Ablation gaps are modest and single-run, with no variance reported.
Memory stores everything for the whole episode, so it grows unbounded. Efficient writing or capacity limits are left as future work.
Idealized setting: no sensing, control or communication delay errors; simulation only, and the dataset uses only 25/5/5 Gibson-tiny scenes for train/val/test.
builds_on: Active Neural SLAM / Object Goal Navigation map module
